## 2

I understand why some people find that idea persuasive, especially when institutions and governments have sometimes misled the public. But the evidence for a round Earth doesn’t depend on trusting space agencies or photographs. Ships disappear hull-first over the horizon, Earth’s shadow on the Moon during lunar eclipses is consistently round, different stars are visible at different latitudes, and people can circumnavigate the planet. Satellites, GPS, weather forecasting, and amateur high-altitude observations also depend on a spherical Earth. Photos can be edited, but these independent observations all point to the same conclusion.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors mixed together. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Blue light gets scattered in many directions more strongly than most of the other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from all across the sky.

Violet is scattered even more, but our eyes are less sensitive to violet, and some violet light is absorbed high in the atmosphere. That is why the sky usually looks blue. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, which scatters away much of the blue and leaves more reds, oranges, and pinks for us to see.

雨下了一整夜，像一层细密的帘子，把城市轻轻隔在朦胧之外。路灯在积水里晃动，碎成一片片金色的光。屋檐不断滴水，声音清脆而有节奏，仿佛有人在黑暗中敲着小鼓。偶尔一辆汽车驶过，轮胎卷起水花，很快又消失在街角。窗边的猫安静地蜷着，玻璃上凝着水雾。我泡了一杯热茶，听着雨声，忽然觉得这个漫长的夜晚也并不孤单。
